effect_estimate.comment: PDF text extraction omits minus signs in numeric tables, so signs are verified directly against the author's prose in Section 6(a)–(c) (e.g., increases in improved water sources and decreases in river water use).
effect_estimate.value: In modified difference-in-differences regressions (program village × no prior title, N = 3,182 households), the PETT land-titling program increased use of an improved water source by 5.9 percentage points (0.059, SE = 0.027, p < 0.05), reduced river water use by 4.3 percentage points (magnitude 0.043, SE = 0.024, p < 0.10; no significant change in tanker truck/vendor use: 0.005, SE = 0.009), and increased public sanitation or septic system access by 15.1 percentage points (0.151, SE = 0.0347, p < 0.01). For realizing a public network connection within the 5 years prior to the survey (proxying utility/government investment), PETT increased public water network connections by 3.2 percentage points (0.032, SE = 0.019, p < 0.10) and public sanitation network connections by 15.1 percentage points (0.151, SE = 0.035, p < 0.01). Households showed no statistically significant out-of-pocket or credit investment in public water connections (amount invested 6.212 S./, SE = 7.794; used own resources 0.019, SE = 0.018; used credit 0.004, SE = 0.004) and no significant difference in monthly water payments, whereas use of own financial resources for sanitation connections increased by 2.4 percentage points (0.024, SE = 0.009, p < 0.01).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 9, Section 6(a) and Table 5; PDF pp. 9–11, Section 6(b) and Table 6

mechanism_certainty.comment: Quasi-experimental intention-to-treat double-difference design (phased village rollout × lack of pre-existing non-PETT title) appraised with ROBINS-I at Moderate overall risk of bias: region fixed effects, within-village differencing against prior-titled households, PSM-DD common-support robustness check, connection-year vs. PETT-timing check (only 3 reported water connection dates predated PETT), and null placebo tests on non-utility community services (police stations, clean parks, clean public areas, public phones) support Moderate rather than Serious RoB despite relying on a single post-rollout cross-sectional survey without pre-intervention panel waves. Downstream government/utility vs. household investment sub-channels rely on survey proxies (recent 5-year connections and household financing reports).

mechanism_flags.comment: Evaluates formal property rights and land tenure security via formal land-title documentation (ELIGIBILITY: tenure, property, documentation) under Peru's PETT program, which removed costly registration fees, bureaucratic hurdles/procedures, and long registration periods (BURDEN: fees, procedural_steps, delay), alongside empirical analysis of upfront connection costs/fees and monthly water fees.
